entry.title: Building an Interactive 3D Experience with Three.js and React for Schildr
entry.summary:
Hey Dev Community! 👋 I’ve been working on a project where I combined Three.js with React to create an interactive 3D experience. This is something I’m really excited to share, and I’d love to get some feedback and tips from all of you! The Project: Schildr The project is built for schildr.com, with a focus on the Configure Yourself section, where users can interact with 3D visualizations.
What is Schildr? Schildr is a platform that lets you customize and configure products in a 3D space, and I had the chance to take part in building the 3D visualization component of the experience. The goal was to make the customization process not only functional but also visually engaging, and that’s where Three.js comes in. The Tech Stack React: To build the front-end and handle state management. Three.js: For creating the 3D scenes, rendering, and adding interactive elements. React-Three-Fiber: A powerful React renderer for Three.js, which made the integration smooth and helped me manage 3D scenes directly within the React component tree. Styled Components: To handle the CSS styling for the React components. Key Features 3D Product Customization
Smooth Animations
Optimized for Performance
Challenges & Solutions Managing 3D Scene in React Performance Tuning
Why Three.js + React? The combination of Three.js and React is incredibly powerful for building interactive and visually rich user interfaces. React provides a solid structure for managing the UI, while Three.js gives you the flexibility to create detailed and engaging 3D content. By using React-Three-Fiber, the two technologies work together like a charm, and the experience is super responsive. Check It Out! Feel free to explore the project at https://schildr.com and take a look at the Configure Yourself section for the full experience. If you have any suggestions or feedback, I’d love to hear it!

entry.title: Why GraphQL Adoption Keeps Growing: Benefits and Limitations
entry.summary: REST has been the default method for designing APIs for years. It's predictable, resource-oriented, and simple enough that nearly every engineering team has used it. However, as applications grew more complex, their shortcomings became increasingly difficult to overlook. Mobile clients wanted lighter payloads. Single-page apps needed flexible queries. Teams found themselves battling over-fetching, under-fetching, and endless endpoint versions to keep features moving. GitHub, Shopify, and Netflix rely on GraphQL in production to simplify API use and scale effectively. Adoption continues to grow because GraphQL addresses recurring problems in distributed systems. In Week 5 of my Open Source Development course, the task was to add a new feature to another student’s repository. I decided to work on the project Repository-Context-Packager. entry.title: The Rise of Ethical AI: Governance Frameworks Every Business Should Know
entry.summary: Introduction As Nate Patel, a technology leader with over 20 years of experience in AI, product, and engineering, often highlights, governance is not just about compliance. It’s about building responsible AI systems that create long-term value, minimize risk, and earn stakeholder trust. His perspectives emphasize that ethical AI is fast becoming a business necessity, not an optional add-on. Why Ethical AI Matters By 2025, nearly 65% of enterprises rank AI governance as their top compliance challenge, while 72% of consumers report they are more likely to trust companies that openly communicate about their AI practices. Here’s a simple comparison: Key Governance Frameworks Every Business Should Know 1. Responsible AI Pillars Model Focuses on fairness, accountability, transparency, and human oversight. These pillars serve as the foundation for any governance plan. 2. Trustworthy AI Lifecycle Framework Outlines governance across the AI lifecycle: Data Collection → Bias Checks → Model Training → Governance Review → Human Oversight → Continuous Monitoring 3. Compliance-by-Design Model Integrates governance checkpoints directly into product development, ensuring AI systems meet regulatory requirements before launch. 4. Adaptive Governance Framework Recognizes that AI and regulations evolve rapidly, so businesses need flexible structures that can adapt without slowing innovation. entry.summary: GitHub Home I remember a few years ago, I was leading a team to develop a real-time stock ticker dashboard. 📈 Initially, everyone's enthusiasm was incredibly high. We were all excited to build a "live" application with our own hands. But soon, we found ourselves stuck in the mud. The tech stack we chose performed reasonably well for ordinary REST APIs, but as soon as WebSockets came into the picture, everything became unrecognizable. Our codebase split into two worlds: the "main application" that handled HTTP requests, and a "separate module" that handled WebSocket connections. Sharing state between these two worlds, like a user's login information, became a nightmare.
